title: Defining Sustainable, Holistic and Inclusive Development

description.x: The lesson plan gives pupils an opportunity to define sustainable, holistic and inclusive development

techniques.x: Case studies, class discussions & Film Screening

objective.x: To introduce the students to the concept of needs vs wants. To understand needs vs wants in the global context. Whose need is more important? Are we living in an inclusive or exclusive society? To help the students individually relook at their needs
To encourage participants to think about what a better quality of life implies (understanding different needs in a society)

materials.x: Pens, Notebooks, Projector, Laptop, Internet, Post Its

sequence.x: Individual Exercise – (5 mins)

Get each of the students to list down their needs without which they cannot survive. This activity needs to be carried out on an individual basis. Give the students a total of 5 minutes to list these needs down in their respective notebooks, or on pieces of paper. Once again, they can choose to be as creative as possible for this activity, and can either simply make a list, or choose to draw out the same.
Film Screening of ‘MAN’ – Steve Cutts – (5 mins)

Screen the short film ‘MAN’ for 5 minutes. It is an animated short film made by Steve Cutts, that looks at mans destructive relationship with natural world, and how we have exploited and depleted our natural resources over the years, in the name of rapid urbanization, industrialization and ‘development’.
Here is the link to the film -- https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qiQU1R0tJUE
Discussion with group based on the activity and observations of the the film
Facilitate a discussion with the group of students recording their observations from the film.

Help them understand how the film showcased a completely opposite definition of sustainable development whereby our natural resources (including our forests, our rivers, our landscapes and our wildlife) were being over exploited and destroyed, at the cost of rapid development. Why is it important to keep a balance between our needs and wants? What will happen to the world, the day we run out of our natural resources? Is this considered good development? Should alternate solutions be addressed and implemented? Is sustainable development important?
Case Study on Kumati –- (10 mins)
IS KUMATI DEVELOPED?

Kumati is a small town with a population of 3,00,000 spread over 50 communities. In a recent survey, the following facts about the town were recorded. Ask the students to Based on your understanding, allot each statement a sign (given below) to decide whether Kumati is a developed town or not.
1. Each community has got a community hospital in the last five years.
2. More than 75% of students have been enrolled in schools. However, only 39% of
them actually go to school.
3. The gross national income of Kumati has increased by 1.5% in the last 7 years.
4. There are only 12 qualified doctors in every community hospital while the required
number is at least 20.
5. The number of deaths due to infectious diseases has gone down by 5% in the last 3
years.
6. In 2012, around 5,000 houses of a community were demolished to build a multiplex.
Till date, they have not been allotted any proper housing.
7. The literacy rate of the city has gone up 1% in the past 2 years.
8. The government has introduced more than 45 new employment schemes. However,
only 19 have been implemented so far.
9. There are wide roads, flyovers and high rise buildings coming up across the town.
10. From 760 girls/ 1000 boys in 2010, the gender ratio has changed to 800 girls /1000
boys in 2014
Would you call Kumati developed or not? Discuss and formulate your collective response in
groups. (10 mins)
OR
Activity – Aladdin’s Lamp

Divide the participants into four groups. Tell one group that they are poor farmers from a small village. The second group are people who live in a slum area in a large city. The third group are housewives in a middle income housing colony. The fourth group are business men in a large city.

Now let them know that each of the groups has stumbled across a magic lamp, which can make their wishes come true. They are allowed to make five wishes for a better quality of life for themselves. The only condition here is that they cannot ask for money. Give them 10 minutes to discuss within their group and come up with 5 wishes that should reflect the roles that they have been assigned.

discussion.x: Concepts of development, sustainable development- intra and inter generational development
Concept of needs v wants
How is the film ‘Man’ connected with the concept of sustainable development? Is there any correlation between them?
Certain things may be a need but still destructive- hence we should use them as efficiently as possible e.g. Electricity or vehicles
Use of plastic –convenience v necessity
Construction of roads, highways through forests- have we thought of a better way to achieve the same goal.
Watering of cricket pitches at the time of drought
Growth of water intensive cash crops over traditional crops
Plantations replacing forest cover
Excessive fisheries, poaching
We don’t want to say that all development is bad but indiscriminate, inefficient and inequitable development should be avoided.
Discussions on Kumati Case Study or Alladin’s Lamp Activity
Concept of economic and social development and their interrelation – one cannot be ignored for the benefit of other
Does economic development guarantee better quality of life
Can it be called economically developed, if one section suffers from extremely low quality of life- refer to terms such as child mortality, maternal mortality, malnutrition, stunting, wasting, etc
Was there a difference in the wishes of the different groups as part of the lamp activity?
What does a better quality of life imply? Is it the same as a better standard of living?
Standard of living refers to our consumption of goods and services, which may or may not guarantee a better quality of life.
What is required to ensure that people have a better quality of life?
How are needs different from wants?
How are our needs different from that of the other groups as mentioned during the ‘lamp activity’?
A better quality of life would require human well being and environmental well being in addition to economic growth.
